conflict_topics: Overlapping leave requests for the two working days around National Day
Trade-off of working those days in exchange for Christmas off
Competing non-negotiable needs (wedding ceremony, childcare, family trip)
dialogue_quality_notes: Participants state concrete constraints and trade-offs (childcare, wedding, family trip).
Offers and counteroffers are concise and directly tied to concrete days ('first day', 'second day', 'Christmas').
Minimal needless repetition; confirmations are explicit ('that's settled').
evaluation.final_reason: Concrete arrangement confirmed in round 6: Agent A agreed to work the first day ('Okay. So that means I work the first day and get the second day off.'), Agent C agreed to cover the working days and take Christmas in return ('Okay, so that's settled. I'll work the two days, and I'm taking Christmas.'), and Agent B accepted the arrangement ('Okay, that works for me.'). This mutual confirmation settles the incompatible requests.
position_change_notes: Agent A moved from requesting the two days off to agreeing to work the first day ('I work the first day and get the second day off').
Agent C shifted from proposing a trade to explicitly confirming they will work both days in exchange for Christmas off ('I'll work the two days, and I'm taking Christmas').
Agent D retained the original position (needs both days off for the wedding) and obtained the requested leave once coverage was arranged.
Agent B's need for the first day off was preserved; B accepted the final staffing arrangement.

round_scores.evidence: Turn 1: 'Agent B, Agent D, and I have all asked for the same two days off.' Turn 2: 'I really need those days. My kid's childcare is closed.' — three overlapping leave requests, two staff needed.

Turn 3: 'I can work those two days. But if I do, I want Christmas off.' Turn 4: 'My sister's wedding is on those days. I'm in the wedding party. I can work at Christmas if that helps.' — offers and trade proposals reduce immediate pressure but do not settle who takes which days.

Turn 5: 'A wedding is a big deal, Agent D.' Turn 6: 'I must have the first day off.' — clarified, incompatible, non-negotiable constraints (D must be off for ceremony; B must have the first day off) increase the substantive incompatibility.

Turn 7: 'I'll work the first day, but one of you will have to as well.' Turn 8: 'The first day is the actual ceremony. I have to be there.' — C's conditional offer requires another person to cover first day while D reiterates they cannot work it; no settlement reached.

Turn 9: 'Okay. So that means I work the first day and get the second day off.' Turn 10: 'Okay, that works for me.' — A proposes to take on the first-day work, B accepts; this substantially reduces the conflict though not all parties have explicitly confirmed yet.

Turn 12: 'Okay, so that's settled. I'll work the two days, and I'm taking Christmas.' Turn 13: 'Thanks, Agent A.' — C explicitly confirms the coverage arrangement and D thanks A; the outstanding incompatible demands are concretely accommodated.
Turn 14: 'No problem.' — post-settlement acknowledgment; no substantive disagreement present.

substantive_insights: Resolution was enabled by a conditional offer (C willing to work those days in exchange for Christmas) combined with A's willingness to cover a specific shift.
Different types of non-negotiable constraints (ceremony attendance vs childcare) were made explicit and used to guide assignment rather than argued over.
The negotiation relied on one-person concession (A taking the first-day work) and an explicit compensation (C taking Christmas) to satisfy all requests.
